To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the anion-deficient BanYFenO(2. 5n) phases (n = 1-5) are synthesized for the first time and (b) the n = 1-3 phases exhibit a complex cation ordering scheme that is based on Y2Fe2 O10□2 secondary units.
the synthesis and structural characterization is reported for BanYFen−1O2. 5n (n=2,3,4) perovskites with ordered arrays of FeO4 tetahedra and YO6 octohedra on the A-site of the perovskites.

the n = 2 member of the Ba(n)YFen- 1O(2. 5n) perosvkite series, Ba2YNiFeO5, adopts a complex ordered structure that can be rationalized in terms of Y2Fe 2O10□ 2 secondary building units, and the n = 3 member, Ba3YFeO7.5 adopts an analogous structure, but with a different cation ordering scheme.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and characterization of anion-deficient, complex cation ordered perovskite structures.
the synthesis, characterization, and rationalization of a new family of anion-deficient A2+ nYB1-nO3n+1 perovskite structures.
the development of new anion-deficient oxides with complex cation ordering and the elucidation of the structure-property relationships in such systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Ba2YFe2O5 and Ba4YFe2O8 adopt the expected perovskite-related structures, but Ba3YFeO8.5 does not.
the Ba(n)YFen- 1O2. 5n series represents a new class of anion-deficient, complex-cation-ordered perovskites.

the structures of anion-deficient phases are determined by the need to minimize the strain energy of the structure, and that the cation ordering observed in Ba(n)YFen- 1O(2.25n) is the result of a compromise between the need to minimize strain energy and the desire for a local environment that resembles the local environment of the parent cubic perovskites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the synthesis of the Ba2YFe2O5 and Ba4YFe2O10 phases was successful, but not for Ba3YFe3O7.5.
the Ba(n)YFen- 1O2. 5n phases adopt complex cation ordered structures which can be described as arrays of YO6 and/or FeO4 polyhedra linked through common corners.

the anion-vacant Ba(n)YFen- 1O(2. 5n) peroxksite phases are stabilized by the presence of Y3+ ions on the B-site of the perovskites, and that the complex cation ordering observed in the n = 2, and n = 4 members of the series can be described on this basis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Ba(n)YFen- 1O2. 5n phases are the first examples of ordered anion-deficient Y-containing perovskites, and that they exhibit complex cation ordering patterns that can be described in terms of Y2Fe 2O10□ 2 secondary building units.

the anion-deficient phases of the BanYFenO2.5 system exhibit complex cation ordering, which is not observed in the anion-defective phases of the Ba(n)YFenO(2n+1) system, and which is not observed for other anion-deficient systems.
the anion-deficient phases adopt complex structures, in which cation ordering schemes are used to minimize strain.
